audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for weak/strong, food/days, nonjudgment, Lordship, conscience, kingdom as justice/peace/joy, not causing stumbling.

verses.restored: Receive the one weak in trust, not into disputes of reasonings.

familiar.text: Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.

modern.text: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.

original.text: Τὸν δὲ ἀσθενοῦντα τῇ πίστει προσλαμβάνεσθε, μὴ εἰς διακρίσεις διαλογισμῶν.

verses.restored: One trusts to eat all things, but the weak one eats vegetables.

familiar.text: For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs.

modern.text: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.

original.text: ὃς μὲν πιστεύει φαγεῖν πάντα, ὁ δὲ ἀσθενῶν λάχανα ἐσθίει.

verses.restored: Let the one eating not despise the one not eating, and let the one not eating not judge the one eating, for the Divine received that one.

familiar.text: Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him.

modern.text: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.

original.text: ὁ ἐσθίων τὸν μὴ ἐσθίοντα μὴ ἐξουθενείτω, ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ μὴ ἐσθίων τὸν ἐσθίοντα μὴ κρινέτω, ὁ θεὸς γὰρ αὐτὸν προσελάβετο.

verses.restored: Who are you judging another's household servant? To one's own lord one stands or falls; and that one will be made to stand, for the Lord is powerful to make that one stand.

familiar.text: Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

modern.text: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.

original.text: σὺ τίς εἶ ὁ κρίνων ἀλλότριον οἰκέτην; τῷ ἰδίῳ κυρίῳ στήκει ἢ πίπτει· σταθήσεται δέ, ⸂δυνατεῖ γὰρ⸃ ὁ ⸀κύριος στῆσαι αὐτόν.

verses.restored: One judges one day above another; another judges every day alike. Let each be fully assured in one's own mind.

familiar.text: One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.

modern.text: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.

original.text: Ὃς ⸀μὲν κρίνει ἡμέραν παρʼ ἡμέραν, ὃς δὲ κρίνει πᾶσαν ἡμέραν· ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ νοῒ πληροφορείσθω·

verses.restored: The one minding the day minds it to the Lord; and the one eating eats to the Lord, for that one gives thanks to the Divine; and the one not eating abstains to the Lord and gives thanks to the Divine.

familiar.text: He that regardeth the day, regardeth it unto the Lord; and he that regardeth not the day, to the Lord he doth not regard it. He that eateth, eateth to the Lord, for he giveth God thanks; and he that eateth not, to the Lord he eateth not, and giveth God thanks.

modern.text: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.

original.text: ὁ φρονῶν τὴν ἡμέραν κυρίῳ ⸀φρονεῖ. καὶ ὁ ἐσθίων κυρίῳ ἐσθίει, εὐχαριστεῖ γὰρ τῷ θεῷ· καὶ ὁ μὴ ἐσθίων κυρίῳ οὐκ ἐσθίει, καὶ εὐχαριστεῖ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: For none of us lives to oneself, and none dies to oneself.

familiar.text: For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself.

modern.text: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.

original.text: Οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἑαυτῷ ζῇ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἑαυτῷ ἀποθνῄσκει·

verses.restored: For if we live, we live to the Lord; and if we die, we die to the Lord. Therefore whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.

familiar.text: For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord’s.

modern.text: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

original.text: ἐάν τε γὰρ ζῶμεν, τῷ κυρίῳ ζῶμεν, ἐάν τε ἀποθνῄσκωμεν, τῷ κυρίῳ ἀποθνῄσκομεν. ἐάν τε οὖν ζῶμεν ἐάν τε ἀποθνῄσκωμεν, τοῦ κυρίου ἐσμέν.

verses.restored: For to this Messiah died and lived, so that he might be Lord of both dead and living.

familiar.text: For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living.

modern.text: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.

original.text: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ⸀Χριστὸς ⸀ἀπέθανεν καὶ ἔζησεν ἵνα καὶ νεκρῶν καὶ ζώντων κυριεύσῃ.

verses.restored: But you, why do you judge your sibling? Or you also, why do you despise your sibling? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of the Divine.

familiar.text: But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

modern.text: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.

original.text: Σὺ δὲ τί κρίνεις τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; ἢ καὶ σὺ τί ἐξουθενεῖς τὸν ἀδελφόν σου; πάντες γὰρ παραστησόμεθα τῷ βήματι τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ,

verses.restored: For it has been written: As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bend to me, and every tongue will confess to the Divine.

familiar.text: For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God.

modern.text: It is written: “As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”

original.text: γέγραπται γάρ· Ζῶ ἐγώ, λέγει κύριος, ὅτι ἐμοὶ κάμψει πᾶν γόνυ, καὶ ⸂πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσεται⸃ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: So then each of us will give account concerning oneself to the Divine.

familiar.text: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.

modern.text: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God. The Law of Love (Ezekiel 14:1–11; 1 Corinthians 8:1–13)

original.text: ⸀ἄρα ἕκαστος ἡμῶν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ λόγον ⸀δώσει.

verses.restored: Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but judge this rather: not to place stumbling block or snare before the sibling.

familiar.text: Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother’s way.

modern.text: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.

original.text: Μηκέτι οὖν ἀλλήλους κρίνωμεν· ἀλλὰ τοῦτο κρίνατε μᾶλλον, τὸ μὴ τιθέναι πρόσκομμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἢ σκάνδαλον.

verses.restored: I know and am persuaded in Lord Jesus that nothing is common through itself, except to the one calculating something common, to that one it is common.

familiar.text: I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

modern.text: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.

original.text: οἶδα καὶ πέπεισμαι ἐν κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ ὅτι οὐδὲν κοινὸν διʼ ⸀ἑαυτοῦ· εἰ μὴ τῷ λογιζομένῳ τι κοινὸν εἶναι, ἐκείνῳ κοινόν.

verses.restored: For if because of food your sibling is grieved, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Messiah died.

familiar.text: But if thy brother be grieved with thy meat, now walkest thou not charitably. Destroy not him with thy meat, for whom Christ died.

modern.text: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.

original.text: εἰ ⸀γὰρ διὰ βρῶμα ὁ ἀδελφός σου λυπεῖται, οὐκέτι κατὰ ἀγάπην περιπατεῖς. μὴ τῷ βρώματί σου ἐκεῖνον ἀπόλλυε ὑπὲρ οὗ Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.

verses.restored: Therefore do not let your good be spoken of as harmful.

familiar.text: Let not then your good be evil spoken of:

modern.text: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.

original.text: μὴ βλασφημείσθω οὖν ὑμῶν τὸ ἀγαθόν.

verses.restored: For the reign of the Divine is not eating and drinking, but righteousness/justice and peace and joy in holy Spirit.

familiar.text: For the kingdom of God is not meat and drink; but righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

original.text: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ βρῶσις καὶ πόσις, ἀλλὰ δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ χαρὰ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ·

verses.restored: For the one serving Messiah in this is pleasing to the Divine and approved by humans.

familiar.text: For he that in these things serveth Christ is acceptable to God, and approved of men.

modern.text: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ ἐν ⸀τούτῳ δουλεύων τῷ Χριστῷ εὐάρεστος τῷ θεῷ καὶ δόκιμος τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.

verses.restored: So then let us pursue the things of peace and the things of building up one another.

familiar.text: Let us therefore follow after the things which make for peace, and things wherewith one may edify another.

modern.text: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.

original.text: ἄρα οὖν τὰ τῆς εἰρήνης διώκωμεν καὶ τὰ τῆς οἰκοδομῆς τῆς εἰς ἀλλήλους.

verses.restored: Do not tear down the work of the Divine because of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is harmful for a human to eat through stumbling.

familiar.text: For meat destroy not the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but it is evil for that man who eateth with offence.

modern.text: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.

original.text: μὴ ἕνεκεν βρώματος κατάλυε τὸ ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ. πάντα μὲν καθαρά, ἀλλὰ κακὸν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ διὰ προσκόμματος ἐσθίοντι.

verses.restored: It is beautiful/good not to eat flesh nor drink wine nor do anything by which your sibling stumbles.

familiar.text: It is good neither to eat flesh, nor to drink wine, nor any thing whereby thy brother stumbleth, or is offended, or is made weak.

modern.text: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.

original.text: καλὸν τὸ μὴ φαγεῖν κρέα μηδὲ πιεῖν οἶνον μηδὲ ἐν ᾧ ὁ ἀδελφός σου προσκόπτει ⸂ἢ σκανδαλίζεται ἢ ἀσθενεῖ⸃·

verses.restored: The trust that you have, have according to yourself before the Divine. Blessed/flourishing is the one not judging oneself in what one approves.

familiar.text: Hast thou faith? have it to thyself before God. Happy is he that condemneth not himself in that thing which he alloweth.

modern.text: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.

original.text: σὺ πίστιν ⸀ἣν ἔχεις κατὰ σεαυτὸν ἔχε ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ. μακάριος ὁ μὴ κρίνων ἑαυτὸν ἐν ᾧ δοκιμάζει·

verses.restored: But the one doubting, if eating, has been condemned, because it is not from trust; and everything that is not from trust is sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: And he that doubteth is damned if he eat, because he eateth not of faith: for whatsoever is not of faith is sin.

modern.text: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

original.text: ὁ δὲ διακρινόμενος ἐὰν φάγῃ κατακέκριται, ὅτι οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως· πᾶν δὲ ὃ οὐκ ἐκ πίστεως ἁμαρτία ⸀ἐστίν.

translation_notes: Romans 14 is about conscience, table fellowship, and non-destruction of siblings, not universalizing one group's scruples.
Koinos/common language is preserved carefully: Paul says nothing is common in itself, yet conscience matters.
